written.myAnswer: Sodium has the maximum atomic radius, and argon has the minimum atomic radius in the third period.

The first ionization energy of magnesium is lower because, after one electron is removed, the remaining electron in Mg⁺ experiences stronger attraction to the nucleus and requires more energy to remove.
Cesium has the lowest ionization energy, and fluorine has the highest electronegativity.
Aluminum loses electrons more easily because its outer electrons are farther from the nucleus and less strongly attracted than boron’s.
The atomic radius is half the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded atoms.

Across a period, atomic radius generally decreases because nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell, pulling them closer to the nucleus. Ionization energy generally increases because the outer electrons are held more strongly and require more energy to remove.
